title: iwf-national-iwf-wow-1997
label: Crusher

won.source: WrestleFest '97, 17 March 1997: Crusher pinned Johnny Rage with a small package.

note: Won the IWF National Championship from Johnny Rage at WrestleFest '97; no later document records a further change.

title: iwf-national-iwf-wow-1997
label: Johnny Rage

won.source: The fed's own billing entering WrestleFest '97 (17 March 1997); no document recording the win survives.

note: Lost the IWF National Championship to Crusher at WrestleFest '97 after a long absence from the ring.

title: iwf-us-iwf-wow-1997
label: "King" Kevin Payne

won.source: The fed's own billing entering WrestleFest '97 (17 March 1997); no document recording the win survives.

note: Retained the IWF United States Championship against Destroyer at WrestleFest '97; no later document records a change.

title: iwf-world-heavyweight-iwf-wow-1997
label: Derrick DaMann

won.source: WrestleFest '97, 17 March 1997: Derrick DaMann pinned AJ "Black Ice" Stanson in the main event.

note: Won the IWF World Heavyweight Championship from AJ "Black Ice" Stanson at WrestleFest '97; no later document records a further change.

title: iwf-world-heavyweight-iwf-wow-1997
label: AJ "Black Ice" Stanson

won.source: The fed's own billing entering WrestleFest '97 (17 March 1997); no document recording the win survives.

note: Lost the IWF World Heavyweight Championship to Derrick DaMann in the main event of WrestleFest '97.

title: wow-world-heavyweight-iwf-wow-1997
label: Jeremy "Roadkill" Thranton

won.source: WrestleFest '97, 17 March 1997: Jeremy Thranton pinned the Prophet.

note: Won the WOW World Heavyweight Championship from the Prophet at WrestleFest '97, weeks after coming up short against Martin Richards for the North American title.

title: wow-world-heavyweight-iwf-wow-1997
label: The Prophet

won.source: The fed's own billing entering WrestleFest '97 (17 March 1997); no document recording the win survives.

note: Lost the WOW World Heavyweight Championship to Jeremy "Roadkill" Thranton at WrestleFest '97.

title: iwf-wow-north-american-iwf-wow-1997
label: Jedah the Damned

won.source: WrestleFest II, 22 March 1998: wins the Damned Alter match over David Pietka

note: No document in the held record records how this reign ended; by End of the World II (18 May 1998) the title is contested as vacant in a twenty-man battle royal, with Jedah not among the entrants.

title: iwf-wow-world-tag-team-iwf-wow-1997
label: Lethal Leaders

won.source: New Year's Mayhem, 1-2 January 1998: outlasts the Bionic Team and Horror in a four-way title elimination match

note: Retained the title over Horror in a no-disqualification match at WrestleFest II before losing it to Alex Extreme and Magnus Colby in a four-corners match at End of the World II.

title: iwf-wow-north-american-tag-team-iwf-wow-1997
label: Helter Skelter

won.source: WrestleFest '97, 17 March 1997: Helter Skelter (Rex Rock and Casper) won the tournament final over Horror, becoming the first champions.

note: Became the first IWF/WOW North American Tag Team Champions at WrestleFest '97.

title: iwf-wow-world-heavyweight-unified-iwf-wow-1997
label: Christopher Stonebreaker

won.source: WrestleFest II, 22 March 1998: wins after America's Least Wanted turns on the Prophet, whose own superkick-dodge sends Joe Kidd's kick into his champion by mistake

note: Retained the title at End of the World II (four corners) and at Summer Explosion III over Robert d'Artois before losing it to the Idol on Friday Night WARFARE, wrestling under a biased special guest referee and enforcer.

title: iwf-wow-intercontinental-iwf-wow-1997
label: "Downtown" Doug Sullivan

won.source: billed the promotion's own new Intercontinental Champion on its 24 February 1998 broadcast

note: Lost the title to the Idol by the time of End of the World II (18 May 1998); no document in the held record records that title change. Challenged unsuccessfully to reclaim the title at End of the World II itself.

title: iwf-wow-us-national-iwf-wow-1997
label: Cooper Concrete

won.source: Monday Mayhem, 28 July 1998

note: Held the title through the promotion's own 25 October 1998 rankings bulletin (the last held in the held record); the promotion's own periodic bulletin the following August instead bills Scotty Phillips as US National Champion and Cooper Concrete himself as World Heavyweight Champion, with no surviving document narrating either transition.

title: iwf-wow-world-tag-team-iwf-wow-1997
label: Dynamic Duo

won.source: End of the World II, 18 May 1998: wins a four-corners match also involving the Lethal Leaders, the Killing Machines and Horror

note: Lost the title to the Killing Machines in a four-corners match, also involving the Lethal Leaders and the Circle of Death, at Summer Explosion III.

title: iwf-wow-world-heavyweight-unified-iwf-wow-1997
label: The Idol

won.source: Friday Night WARFARE, broadcast dateline 30 October 1998: pins Christopher Stonebreaker with the Peace Crusher

note: No further document in the held record records this reign's own end; the promotion's own periodic bulletin of 4 August 1999 instead bills Cooper Concrete as IWF/WOW World Heavyweight Champion, with no surviving document narrating the transition.

title: iwf-wow-world-heavyweight-unified-iwf-wow-1997
label: Cooper Concrete

won.source: The promotion's own repeated billing, most recently its periodic bulletin of 4 August 1999, naming him the reigning IWF/WOW World Heavyweight Champion.

note: Recorded from the promotion's own repeated billing rather than a surviving title-change document.

title: iwf-wow-world-heavyweight-unified-iwf-wow-1997
label: The Prophet

won.source: already the billed three-time IWF/WOW World Champion entering New Year's Mayhem (1-2 January 1998); no document in the held record records this reign's own start

note: Retained the title over AJ Stanson at New Year's Mayhem after Derek McMasters's interference, then lost it to Christopher Stonebreaker at WrestleFest II when America's Least Wanted turned on him mid-match.

title: iwf-wow-us-national-iwf-wow-1997
label: "Black Feather" Scotty Phillips

won.source: The promotion's own repeated billing, most recently its periodic bulletin of 4 August 1999, naming him the reigning IWF/WOW US National Champion.

note: Recorded from the promotion's own repeated billing rather than a surviving title-change document.

title: iwf-wow-us-national-iwf-wow-1997
label: "Top Dog" Rick Styles

won.source: already billed the IWF/WOW US National Champion (addressed on-air by the Prophet as "our new US National Champion, Brother Styles") entering New Year's Mayhem; no document in the held record records this reign's own start

note: Stripped of the title in the course of the New Year's Mayhem broadcast itself (1-2 January 1998); the broadcast never states why, and the planned title-for-title match this cost is reduced to an Intercontinental-only match that is itself cancelled when the champion walks out with the belt.

title: iwf-wow-us-national-iwf-wow-1997
label: "Professor" Steve West

won.source: billed the IWF/WOW US National Champion entering WrestleFest II (22 March 1998); no document in the held record records this reign's own start

note: Retained the title over Shane Sanders in a lumberjack match at WrestleFest II after Andros's interference, then lost it to Slade Waters by the time of End of the World II; no document in the held record records that title change.

title: iwf-wow-us-national-iwf-wow-1997
label: "Stuntman" Slade Waters

won.source: billed the IWF/WOW US National Champion entering End of the World II (18 May 1998); no document in the held record records this reign's own start

note: Retained the title over Steve West by submission at End of the World II, then lost it to Eric Travers by 26 July 1998; no document in the held record records that title change.

title: iwf-wow-us-national-iwf-wow-1997
label: "Epic" Eric Travers

won.source: billed the IWF/WOW US National Champion on the promotion's own 26 July 1998 rankings bulletin; no document in the held record records this reign's own start

note: Lost the title to Cooper Concrete on Monday Mayhem two days later (28 July 1998).

title: iwf-wow-north-american-iwf-wow-1997
label: "Hot Stuff" Alex Martinez

won.source: End of the World II, 18 May 1998: wins a twenty-man battle royal for the vacant title, eliminating Johnny Skiles last

note: Lost the title to Johnny Skiles in the sixth and final fall of the Four Way Revenge match at Summer Explosion III.

title: iwf-wow-north-american-iwf-wow-1997
label: "Legacy" Johnny Skiles

won.source: Summer Explosion III, 31 August 1998: rolls up Alex Martinez in the sixth and final fall of the Four Way Revenge match

note: Lost the title to Vincent Bannister on Friday Night WARFARE.

title: iwf-wow-north-american-iwf-wow-1997
label: Vincent Bannister

won.source: Friday Night WARFARE, broadcast dateline 30 October 1998

note: No later document in the held record records a further change; the promotion's own 1999 periodic bulletin does not mention this title.

title: iwf-wow-north-american-iwf-wow-1997
label: "Trouble Man" Martin Richards

won.source: The fed's own billing entering WrestleFest '97 (17 March 1997); no document recording the win survives.

note: Retained the IWF/WOW North American Championship against the Desert Scorpion at WrestleFest '97 when both men were counted out; the title later changed hands during 1998, though no document in the held record records the exact match.

title: iwf-wow-north-american-iwf-wow-1997
label: Dan "The Man" Watterson

won.source: billed on a WrestleFest II broadcast segment as a past IWF/WOW North American Champion, preceding David Pietka's own reign; no document in the held record records this reign's own start or end

note: A thinly attested reign, named only in passing by a rival on a WrestleFest-era broadcast; no card recording either its start or its loss survives in the held record.

title: iwf-wow-north-american-iwf-wow-1997
label: "Darkseid" David Pietka

won.source: billed the IWF/WOW North American Champion entering WrestleFest II (22 March 1998); no document in the held record records this reign's own start

note: Lost the title to Jedah the Damned in a Damned Alter match at WrestleFest II.

title: iwf-wow-intercontinental-iwf-wow-1997
label: AJ "Black Ice" Stanson

won.source: Summer Explosion III, 31 August 1998: pins the Idol in the fifth fall of the Four Way Revenge match, in a finish the broadcast itself frames as pre-arranged between the two men

note: Retained the title over Steve West on Friday Night WARFARE; no further document in the held record records this reign's own end. The promotion's own periodic bulletin of 4 August 1999 instead bills Razor Ron Jeremy as Intercontinental Champion, with no surviving document narrating the transition.

title: iwf-wow-intercontinental-iwf-wow-1997
label: "Razor" Ron Jeremy

won.source: The promotion's own repeated billing, most recently its periodic bulletin of 4 August 1999, naming him the reigning IWF/WOW Intercontinental Champion.

note: Recorded from the promotion's own repeated billing rather than a surviving title-change document.

title: iwf-wow-intercontinental-iwf-wow-1997
label: The Idol

won.source: billed the IWF/WOW Intercontinental Champion entering End of the World II (18 May 1998); no document in the held record records this reign's own start

note: Retained the title over Doug Sullivan at End of the World II, then lost it to AJ Stanson in a worked, collusive finish during the sixth-fall Four Way Revenge match at Summer Explosion III.

title: iwf-wow-world-tag-team-iwf-wow-1997
label: Killing Machines

won.source: Summer Explosion III, 31 August 1998

note: Retained the title over the West Coast Connection on Friday Night WARFARE; no later document in the held record records a further change. The promotion's own periodic bulletin of 4 August 1999 instead bills Fusion and Alex Cote as World Tag Team Champions, with no surviving document narrating the transition.

title: iwf-wow-world-tag-team-iwf-wow-1997
label: Body Count

won.source: The fed's own billing entering WrestleFest '97 (17 March 1997); no document recording the win survives.

note: Retained the IWF/WOW World Tag Team Championship against America's Least Wanted at WrestleFest '97.

title: iwf-wow-world-tag-team-iwf-wow-1997
label: Fusion & Alex Cote

won.source: The promotion's own repeated billing, most recently its periodic bulletin of 4 August 1999, naming them the reigning IWF/WOW World Tag Team Champions.

note: Recorded from the promotion's own repeated billing rather than a surviving title-change document; the previously held Body Count reign carries no recorded end in the held record.

title: iwf-wow-world-tag-team-iwf-wow-1997
label: America's Least Wanted

won.source: billed the IWF/WOW World Tag Team Champions entering New Year's Mayhem, having "ended the career of Body Count"; no document in the held record records this reign's own start

note: Eliminated first by the Bionic Team in the four-way title elimination match at New Year's Mayhem; the title passes to the match's ultimate winner, the Lethal Leaders, rather than to the Bionic Team.
